title: Hollis & Vane — a design studio for public services
description: An eight-person studio that designs the services people have to use: council tax, school places, hospital letters. Brand, product and the systems behind them.

parking.title: Resident parking
parking.summary: A permit in four minutes instead of four weeks, for a city of 300,000.

media.alt: The permit flow on a phone: one question per screen

admissions.title: School admissions
admissions.summary: One form for every school in the county, with the deadline on every page.

media.alt: A ranked list of six schools, the first one highlighted

letters.title: Outpatient letters
letters.summary: Hospital letters rewritten so the time, the place and what to bring come first.

media.alt: A hospital letter with the appointment set large at the top

bins.title: Bin day
bins.summary: One text the night before, for 140,000 homes: which bin, and only when it changes.

wayfinding.title: Library wayfinding
wayfinding.summary: Signs, a type family and an app for eleven branch libraries.

media.alt: A tall library sign with floor numbers in a bold sans

sections.title: Forms nobody dreads.
sections.lede: Council tax, school places, hospital letters: the services people have no choice but to use, made clear enough to use once and forget.

sections.title: Resident parking, in four minutes
sections.body: The old permit took a printed form, two proofs of address and a four-week wait. We rebuilt it around the one thing the council already knew: where you live. Most residents now finish before the kettle boils.

media.alt: The parking permit confirmation screen beside the old paper form

sections.title: Studio
sections.body: Most of the work happens on paper, on the wall, and in the rooms where the service is used.

media.alt: Paper prototypes of a form, laid out across a table
A wall of printed screens with handwritten notes
A library sign prototype propped against a shelf
Type specimens pinned in a grid
A research session in a council reception, seen from behind
A notebook open on a grid page of letter layouts

items.text: They spent the first week in our reception, not in a workshop. That week is why the service works.
items.role: Head of digital, a city council

items.text: The letters used to generate calls. Now they answer the questions before anyone has to ask.
Our staff stopped printing the guidance, because the screens finally said what the guidance said.

steps.title: Sit where it is used
steps.body: A week in the reception, the call centre or the waiting room, before anything is drawn.

steps.title: Write it plainly
steps.body: The words first: what the service asks, in the order people can answer it.

steps.title: Make it real
steps.body: A working version in the first month, tested with the people who will use it.

steps.title: Hand it over whole
steps.body: Code, a design system and the team trained to keep it, so nobody depends on us.

sections.title: Contact
sections.body: Tell us what it is and who has to use it. We reply within two working days, with a first idea.

footer.note: An eight-person studio in Leeds. We work in the open: our design system and research methods are public.
